question: Can a tiny obstacle/support/boundary/depth interaction head provide parent-disjoint two-sided obstacle evidence when its thresholds are calibrated only from inner out-of-parent predictions?

protocol.head: standardized_linear_logistic_interaction
protocol.inner_calibration: Each calibration parent was predicted by a head fitted on the other four outer-training parents.
protocol.outer_evaluation: Each held parent was predicted once by a head fitted on the other five parents.

result.interpretation: The interaction head did not produce a complete inner-out-of-parent threshold pair for any outer fold. Combining the frozen RGB factor logits, base depth topology and image-row prior therefore did not repair cross-parent conditional reliability.

decision.next_successor_scope: Test one new representation rather than another learned-score selector. On the same consumed six-parent pool, use frozen DepthART RGB+K metric depth plus source-native camera_to_world as a runtime-equivalent pose/gravity input. Recover the lowest persistent horizontal world-height mode from predicted depth only, derive per-frame camera height and analytic obstacle probability with the frozen factor geometry, map invalid analytic evidence to UNKNOWN, then run parent-LOO tri-state calibration under the unchanged per-parent false-negative, false-positive and two-sided coverage gates. Source depth, source factor truth and task outcomes remain unopened until every analytic candidate is complete.

claim_boundary: Consumed Development evidence that a tiny interaction head over the current R21 RGB factor observables cannot safely land obstacle evidence. It closes further selectors over that observable family and authorizes one pose-anchored analytic representation canary only; it does not establish task utility, independent cross-sensor generalization, deployment, product readiness, default-App eligibility, navigation utility or assistive safety.
